chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated, saying: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:

“When you depart from Mecca to Medina and reach Dhū al-Ḥulayfah while returning to Medina from Mecca, then go to the Muʿarras of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. If you are in the time of an obligatory salat or a supererogatory prayer, then perform salat. And if it is not the time of salat, then dismount there for a little while, for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله used to halt there and perform salat there.”

key_terms.ذِي ٱلْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, the location reached on the return route to Medina
key_terms.مُعَرَّسَ: the resting place or halting place where the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله would stop
key_terms.يُعَرِّسُ: he would halt and rest there

ai.seo_question: What should one do at the Muʿarras of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله when returning from Mecca to Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs the traveler returning from Mecca to Medina to stop at the Muʿarras of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله near Dhū al-Ḥulayfah. It recommends performing salat there if it is prayer time, or otherwise pausing briefly, because this was from the practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.
